slides.headline: October 3, 1978: a Kolkata doctor achieved the world's second-ever IVF birth - alone, with homemade equipment.
Dr. Subhash Mukhopadhyay achieved India's first IVF birth on October 3, 1978, in Kolkata
slides.body: The baby, Kanupriya Agarwal, was the world's second IVF baby ever born, just 67 days after the UK's Louise Brown. Mukhopadhyay became only the second physician in the world - and the first in Asia - to achieve a live birth through in-vitro fertilization.

slides.headline: Instead of recognition, he was dismissed and isolated - and never got to see himself vindicated.
slides.body: A state government committee dismissed his claim and barred him from presenting his work internationally. Professionally isolated, Mukhopadhyay died in 1981. It took until 2002 - 21 years after his death - for India's Council of Medical Research to formally recognize his pioneering achievement.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A breakthrough that was real all along doesn't stop being real just because nobody believed it yet.
slides.body: A Viksit Bharat by 2047 needs the institutions that recognize breakthroughs in time - not decades later. Mukhopadhyay's work now stands as one of India's earliest, least-celebrated contributions to reproductive medicine.

sources.text: ThePrint - Subhas Mukherjee pioneered IVF in India but the government refuted his work
